newsitem.title: USA: Kmart Corp corrects international sales.
newsitem.headline: Kmart Corp corrects international sales.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Friday that a clerical error resulted in an underreporting of comparable December sales results in its international operations. Kmart International said same store sales for the five weeks ended January 1 rose 4.8 percent compared with the five-week period ended January 3, 1996.
The Kmart's international business currently includes 125 Canadian stores and four stores operating in Mexico.
Including the international sales results with those of U.S. Kmart stores and Builders Square, Kmart's consolidated same store sales for five-week December period rose 10.8 percent.
On Thursday, Kmart said those same store sales on a consolidated basis rose 10.4 percent.

Comparing the five weeks ended January 1, 1997, against the five weeks ending December 27, 1995, Kmart International comparable sales decreased 7.2 percent due to the inclusion of one post-Christmas week in 1996 versus five pre-Christmas weeks in 1995 under this method.

Kmart said sales for the five weeks ending January 1, 1997, from international operations were $161 million, a decrease of 14.5 percent, compared with sales of $187 million for the five weeks ending January 3, 1996. The decline is entirely due to the divestiture of 13 Czech and Slovak stores and three stores in Singapore in fiscal 1996, it added.
Total sales in Kmart's Canadian operations increased 3.3 percent to US$151 million over the same period.
Sales from international operations for the 48 weeks ended January 1, were $1.0 billion, down 14.4 percent primarily due to divestitures, Kmart said.
On a same store basis, Kmart said its international sales were down 2.9 percent for the 48-week period.
